newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals track world markets higher.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals track world markets higher.

text.p: Indian base metal prices tracked the rise in prices on the world market on Monday, though copper was steady as it consolidated recent gains, trader said.
Copper was unchanged at 13,500 rupees per quintal after gaining 25 rupees on Saturday.
"Other base metals were lifted further on the back of speculative buying influenced by the uptrend in the world market," one broker said.
He said sentiment had been bolstered by expectations that state-owned agencies, looking at the firm trend in world prices, may hike selling prices for August.
Aluminium rose 50 rupees to 7,800 per quintal after gaining 50 rupees on Saturday, while zinc was up 50 rupees at 8,400 and lead gained 25 rupees to 4,200.
Tin climbed 100 rupees to 29,100 per quintal after gaining 500 on Saturday, while nickel rose 300 rupees to 34,100 per quintal after Saturday's gain of 600.
Physical demand for local metals remained dull, but the upsurge in world prices prompted speculative buying and buoyancy at the close of the session.
